From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: EmberOps discovery recap & proposed sizing slots

Hi Samira —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap from my side so we’re aligned before the next step:

- Goal: provision a dedicated GPU pool for real-time embedding + retrieval pipelines and bursty generation workloads.
- Current signals you shared: ~18–25 requests/sec at peak, avg 120–250 tokens per request, occasional spikes to 40 req/s during batch reindex windows.
- Latency target you emphasized: p95 under 350ms for short lookup flows; p95 under 800ms acceptable for longer generation.
- Compliance note: data in-flight must use customer-managed keys (we discussed KMS option).

Next step: schedule a focused \"Capacity Sizing & Throughput Deep Dive\" where Ben (SE) will walk through model variants, pooling recommendations, batching/kv-cache strategies and runway for scaling. To move quickly, can you take a look at these three proposed 60-minute slots?

- Tue 28 Mar, 10:00–11:00 PT
- Wed 29 Mar, 14:00–15:00 PT
- Thu 30 Mar, 09:00–10:00 PT

If none of those work, drop a couple windows that fit your week and we’ll accommodate. I attached a quick discovery-notes PDF from today’s call and a brief prep checklist so Ben can tailor the sizing. Also: if Raj or your infra lead can join, please loop them in — we’ll need traffic profiles and any firewall/VPC constraints ahead of the call.

Thanks,

Tessa Morgan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
T 510-555-0143 | tessa_morgan@redwood.com

Attachment: discovery-notes.pdf (summary of call, redwood action items)

Hi Tessa —

Appreciate the clear recap. Confirming a few details from our side: spikes come from our nightly reindex (roughly 20–30m) and a handful of heavy requests from the analytics pipeline. The numbers you quoted look right.

Raj can join the deep dive — he wants to validate networking and cost assumptions. Of the slots you listed, Wed 29 Mar 14:00 PT works best for us.

I attached a small sample of our traffic (sample_load.csv) — it’s anonymized but shows request size distribution and burst patterns. Two quick questions for the call so Ben can prep:

1) We currently use AES-GCM with KMS for at-rest and would like to use our KMS for in-flight key management — is that supported in Private deployments?
2) Do you recommend starting with a mixed pool (a few fp16 + int8 quantized variants) or spin up separate pools per model for predictable p95 latency?

Samira

Hi Samira / Raj —

Thanks for confirming. Wed 29 Mar, 14:00 PT is confirmed on our side. I created a short agenda and attached a pre-call checklist so we can collect the traffic_profile.csv before the meeting (if possible):

Agenda (60m):
- 5m: intros + success criteria
- 15m: EmberOps traffic profile review (you walk samples)
- 25m: Redwood sizing recommendations (pool configs, batching, quantization)
- 10m: next steps (rollout plan, commit levels, follow-ups)

Pre-call checklist (attached): network egress IPs, VPC peering steps, raw traffic_profile.csv, and the model names/versions you plan to run. If you can drop the traffic_profile.csv in the shared drive or paste a link, that’ll save us time.

Preliminary answers to Samira’s questions:
- KMS: yes — Private supports customer-managed keys; Ben will walk the integration details and required IAM roles during the call.
- Pool strategy: in many cases a single mixed pool with two model variants (quantized + fp16) gives good cost/latency tradeoffs, but we’ll sketch both approaches with estimated p95 outcomes and cost delta.
